subject: general
question: Which era is called golden age of ancient India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Gupta Empire, 4th century**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Gupta Empire, which ruled during the 4th century, is often referred to as the Golden Age of ancient India.
 
• During this period, India witnessed significant achievements in various fields including science, mathematics, astronomy, religion, and philosophy.
 
• Prominent scholars such as Aryabhata and Kalidasa emerged during this era, contributing immensely to their respective fields.
 
• The era was marked by extensive cultural development, including the creation of notable literary and artistic works.
 
• The Gupta period is also known for its advancements in architecture, with the construction of numerous temples and universities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Gupta Empire was founded by Sri Gupta, but it reached its zenith under the reign of Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, and Chandragupta II.
 
• The period saw the codification of laws and the establishment of a centralized administrative system.
 
• Trade and commerce flourished during this time, with the Gupta Empire maintaining robust trade relations with regions such as the Roman Empire and Southeast Asia.
 
• The era also saw the revival and spread of Hinduism, alongside the continued patronage of Buddhism and Jainism.
 
• The Gupta period's contributions to culture, science, and politics have had a lasting impact on Indian civilization.
